en.title: Taiwan: productive concentration, democratic institutions and resilience in a high-dependence island economy
en.deck: Taiwan's semiconductor-centered export model creates exceptional productive capability while imported energy, demographic contraction, infrastructure concentration and cross-Strait pressure make resilience a problem of institutions and physical systems as much as finance.
en.regime: Export-industrial democracy with globally strategic semiconductor concentration, large external buffers and high physical dependence on imported energy, maritime logistics and dense west-coast infrastructure.
en.key_risk: Financial and technological strength cannot substitute for physical continuity if energy, shipping, grid, water or skilled-labor constraints bind simultaneously.
watch: Cross-Strait operational activity without inferring intent from activity alone

pt-BR.title: Taiwan: concentração produtiva, instituições democráticas e resiliência em uma economia insular de alta dependência
pt-BR.deck: O modelo exportador centrado em semicondutores cria capacidade produtiva excepcional, enquanto energia importada, contração demográfica, concentração de infraestrutura e pressão no Estreito tornam resiliência um problema de instituições e sistemas físicos tanto quanto de finanças.
pt-BR.regime: Democracia industrial-exportadora com concentração estratégica global em semicondutores, grandes colchões externos e elevada dependência física de energia importada, logística marítima e infraestrutura densa no corredor oeste.
pt-BR.key_risk: Força financeira e tecnológica não substitui continuidade física se restrições de energia, navegação, rede, água ou trabalho qualificado se tornarem simultaneamente vinculantes.

selection_rationale: The canonical Taiwan Strategic Transition establishes a material mechanism linking semiconductor concentration, external rebalancing, energy dependence, demography, institutions and cross-Strait security. The public corpus still lacks a reusable country-level explanation of how these mechanisms fit together beyond the 2025–2026 transition itself.
contrary_evidence: Exceptional 2026 output and export growth contradict a near-term stagnation thesis but are too concentrated to extrapolate as trend growth.
Overseas semiconductor expansion diversifies geography while simultaneous domestic leading-edge investment contradicts a simple hollowing-out thesis.
Large external buffers reduce financial vulnerability but cannot substitute for maritime energy, grid, water or logistics continuity.
Institutional checks can delay execution without demonstrating generalized state incapacity.
limitations: Taiwan's legal and diplomatic status is contested; the dossier separates effective administration, constitutional claims, recognition and observable relations.
Public military data do not permit precise measurement of readiness, stockpiles or deterrence effects.
Demographic projections are conditional and current population statistics can be affected by registration definitions.
Announced energy and industrial projects are not treated as operating capacity until implementation is documented.
